claim.why_it_matters: Sibling subclauses of 15.5 are split across two markdown levels, so 15.5.3 through 15.5.5 render as peers of 15.5 and of 15.6 rather than as children of 15.5. These are the clauses that define standard date form, Julian date form and standard numeric time form — heavily cross-referenced by the intrinsic-function definitions.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING — the 'missing-heading' kind is factually wrong. All three headings are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md at lines 33736, 33741 and 33746 with the exact clause number and the exact title text: '15.5.3 Standard date form', '15.5.4 Julian date form', '15.5.5 Standard numeric time form'. Every word of page 836's body text is present verbatim as well — verified by substring probe: 'standard date form is YYYYMMDD', 'Julian date form is YYYYDDD', 'seconds past midnight', 'less than 86,400', 'less than 86,401', 'Ord means an ordering table', 'Type means a type declaration', and the closing 'even when all the arguments of the function are of the same type' all match. The 14-line Alph/Anum/Bool/... list, the 15.6 heading and both closing paragraphs are complete and correctly reflowed. Zero text loss on this page. (2) THE PDF DOES NOT ENCODE THE ATTRIBUTE THE CLAIM SAYS WAS LOST. I measured the printed glyphs at 300 dpi rather than trusting my eye — my first visual impression that '15.6' was set larger turned out to be a crop-offset illusion. Figure (digit) height of the clause number: 15.5.3 = 34px, 15.5.5 = 34px, 15.6 = 34px. Cap height of the leading title capital: 'S' of Standard (15.5.3) = 33px, 'S' of Standard (15.5.5) = 33px, 'S' of Summary (15.6) = 33px. Identical size, identical bold weight, identical indent. The ISO PDF therefore carries NO typographic distinction whatsoever between a depth-3 subclause heading and a depth-2 clause heading on this page. The only hierarchy signal the PDF prints is the dotted clause number itself — and that number is transcribed exactly. You cannot have a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy on a property the PDF never expresses; markdown '##' vs '###' depth is an invention of the transcription pipeline, i.e. formatting, which is an explicit rejection criterion. (3) MEANING IS UNCHANGED, INCLUDING FOR THE STATED CONSEQUENCE. The claim's rationale is that these clauses are 'heavily cross-referenced by the intrinsic-function definitions'. Spec cross-references are by clause number ('see 15.5.3'), and the transcription preserves both the literal number in the heading text and a stable explicit anchor (``, likewise -15-5-4 and -15-5-5). Cross-reference resolution and lookup are entirely unaffected by the '#' count. A reader or tool reading '15.5.3' knows it is the third subclause of 15.5 from the number alone. (4) IT IS A SYSTEMIC PAGE-BREAK ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-836 FINDING. The per-page transcription pipeline resets heading depth at each page top. Measured across all 2098 numbered headings in the file: the FIRST numbered heading on a page is level 2 in 505 of 591 cases (85%), while LATER headings on the same page are level 3 in 1199 of 1491 cases (80%). Globally, depth-3 numbering maps to '##' 276 times and '###' 508 times; depth-4 maps to '##' 162 times and '###' 620 times; depth-5 maps to '##' 118 times and '###' 128 times. Page 836's 15.5.3 is precisely the first heading after the '## Page 836' marker, and 15.5.1/15.5.2 on page 835 are mid-page — so the level split the claim reports is exactly the page-break furniture the reconciliation is instructed to reject, reproduced identically on roughly 500 other pages.
verdict.corrected_description:
Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy; reject. No heading and no body text is missing from page 836 — 15.5.3, 15.5.4 and 15.5.5 are all present with exact numbers, exact titles, complete bodies and stable anchors. The PDF sets 15.5.3/15.5.5 (depth 3) and 15.6 (depth 2) in identical type — 34px figures, 33px caps, same bold weight — so the PDF encodes no heading-level distinction for the markdown to lose; hierarchy is carried solely by the dotted clause number, which is transcribed correctly.

Worth recording separately, NOT as a page-836 spec-reconciliation finding: the transcription's markdown heading depths are internally inconsistent document-wide, because the per-page pipeline resets depth at every page top (first-heading-on-page is '##' 85% of the time; later-heading-on-page is '###' 80% of the time; depth-3 numbering splits 276 '##' / 508 '###'). That degrades a generated table of contents and any depth-based section-extraction tooling across the whole file. If the project wants it fixed, the correct remedy is one mechanical document-wide normalization pass setting heading level from the numbering depth (level = number of dot-separated components + 1), not ~500 per-page ledger entries.
